choice: Added an ownership check on `slot_entry` in the workout log API (replacing the dead `session` check), so users can't attach logs to other users' slot entries.
final:
I changed one line in `wger/manager/api/views.py`. The full suite (`python3 manage.py test --settings=settings.ci`) passes: 1418 tests, OK, 17 skipped. I didn't write a test that posts a foreign `slot_entry`, so the new check isn't covered by a test of its own.

The workout log API (`WorkoutLogViewSet`) checks that you own the `routine` you link a log to. It also listed `session`, but the serializer marks `session` read-only, so that check never ran. It never checked `slot_entry`. A user could create or update a log pointing at another user's `SlotEntry` by passing its id. I replaced the `session` entry with `slot_entry`, so a foreign id now gets a 403.

I didn't test this against a running server. I found the gap by reading the code, and I didn't trace everything that reads `slot_entry` on a log. It looks low-impact, since a log only stores the id and logs are filtered per user. Other places that read it, such as the code at `slot_entry.py:426`, may be affected.

The model already blocks the other two cross-user links. `WorkoutLog.save()` drops a log whose routine belongs to someone else and clears a foreign `next_log`.

CHOICE: Added an ownership check on `slot_entry` in the workout log API (replacing the dead `session` check), so users can't attach logs to other users' slot entries.
